questions.q: A vernier calliper has a least count of $C \text{ cm}$. It is given that $N$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $(N-1)$ divisions of the main scale. The number of divisions in $1 \text{ cm}$ on the main scale is
questions.question: A vernier calliper has a least count of $C \text{ cm}$. It is given that $N$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $(N-1)$ divisions of the main scale. The number of divisions in $1 \text{ cm}$ on the main scale is
questions.solution:
The least count (LC) of a vernier calliper is the difference between one main scale division (MSD) and one vernier scale division (VSD).

Given that $N$ VSD = $(N-1)$ MSD, we can write:
$1 \text{ VSD} = \dfrac{N-1}{N} \text{ MSD}$

Therefore, the least count is:
$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ MSD} - 1 \text{ VSD}$
$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ MSD} - \dfrac{N-1}{N} \text{ MSD} = \dfrac{1}{N} \text{ MSD}$

We are given that the least count is $C \text{ cm}$, so:
$\dfrac{1}{N} \text{ MSD} = C \text{ cm}$
$1 \text{ MSD} = N C \text{ cm}$

The number of divisions per cm on the main scale is the reciprocal of the length of one main scale division:
$\text{Number of divisions per cm} = \dfrac{1}{1 \text{ MSD}} = \dfrac{1}{NC}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{NC}$

$N\text{ VSD} = (N-2)\text{ MSD}$

Substitute this into the least count formula:
$\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - \left(\dfrac{N-2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD}$
$\text{LC} = \left(1 - \dfrac{N-2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD}$
$\text{LC} = \left(\dfrac{N - N + 2}{N}\right)\text{ MSD} = \dfrac{2}{N}\text{ MSD}$

We are given that $\text{LC} = x$. Therefore:
$x = \dfrac{2}{N}\text{ MSD}$

Rearranging to find the value of $1\text{ MSD}$:
$1\text{ MSD} = \dfrac{Nx}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Nx}{2}$

questions.question: A telescope observes two points on a distant planet. The linear separation between the points is $\pi \times 10^6 \text{ m}$, and they subtend an angle of $6'$ (minutes of arc) at the telescope. The distance to the planet from the telescope is:
questions.solution:
The plane angle subtended by an arc of length $s$ at a distance $D$ is given by $\theta = \dfrac{s}{D}$, provided $\theta$ is measured in radians.

Given:

$s = \pi \times 10^6 \text{ m}$

$\theta = 6'$

First, convert the angle into radians:

$6' = \left(\dfrac{6}{60}\right)^\circ = 0.1^\circ$

$0.1^\circ = 0.1 \times \dfrac{\pi}{180} \text{ rad} = \dfrac{\pi}{1800} \text{ rad}$

Now, calculate the distance $D$:

$D = \dfrac{s}{\theta} = \dfrac{\pi \times 10^6}{\dfrac{\pi}{1800}}$

$D = 1800 \times 10^6 \text{ m} = 1.8 \times 10^9 \text{ m}$

Answer: $1.8 \times 10^9 \text{ m}$

$1 \text{ MSD} = \dfrac{1}{N} \text{ degrees}$

It is given that $V$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $(V-1)$ divisions of the main scale:
$V \text{ VSD} = (V-1) \text{ MSD}$
$1 \text{ VSD} = \dfrac{V-1}{V} \text{ MSD}$

The least count (LC) is the difference between one MSD and one VSD:
$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ MSD} - 1 \text{ VSD}$
$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ MSD} - \dfrac{V-1}{V} \text{ MSD} = \dfrac{1}{V} \text{ MSD}$

Substituting the value of $1 \text{ MSD}$ in minutes:
$\text{LC} = \dfrac{1}{V} \times \left(\dfrac{60}{N}\right) \text{ minutes} = \dfrac{60}{NV} \text{ minutes}$

Answer: $\dfrac{60}{NV}$

questions.solution:
The least count (LC) of the standard Vernier calliper is:

$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ mm} - 0.9 \text{ mm} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.01 \text{ cm}$

The observed reading during the measurement is:

$\text{Observed reading} = \text{MSR} + (\text{VSR} \times \text{LC}) = 3.1 \text{ cm} + (7 \times 0.01 \text{ cm}) = 3.17 \text{ cm}$

The relationship between actual thickness, observed reading, and zero error is:

$\text{Actual reading} = \text{Observed reading} - \text{Zero error}$

$3.20 \text{ cm} = 3.17 \text{ cm} - \text{Zero error}$

$\text{Zero error} = 3.17 \text{ cm} - 3.20 \text{ cm} = -0.03 \text{ cm}$

For a negative zero error, the zero of the Vernier scale is to the left of the main scale zero. The magnitude of the error is given by:

$\text{Zero error} = -(N - n) \times \text{LC}$

where $N$ is the total number of Vernier divisions ($10$) and $n$ is the coinciding division.

$-0.03 \text{ cm} = -(10 - n) \times 0.01 \text{ cm}$

$10 - n = 3 \implies n = 7$

Thus, the $7^{th}$ Vernier division coincides when the jaws are in contact.

Answer: $7^{th}$
